Run reference-arch design review with Solaris infra team (Jonah) w/in 2 weeks
Send security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence links (Maya) by EOD 2027-11-10
Schedule pilot kickoff & quota for Dedicated capacity testing (Liam + Jonah)
Draft joint solution one-pager for partner portal (Rina)
action_items: Maya Chen: Share marketplace listing draft (due 2027-11-16)
Jonah Patel: Draft reference architecture diagram and perf targets (due 2027-11-23)

header:
Date: 2027-11-09
Time: 15:30 - 17:00 UTC
Duration: 90 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Rina Gomez (Redwood PM); Ava Martinez (SolarisCloud Partner PM), Liam O'Connell (SolarisCloud Cloud Integrations Lead), Priya Nair (SolarisCloud Security Architect)
Recording: cloud-recording-link://redwood/ff/987654
summary: Partner sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint solution (SolarisCloud managed marketplace offering + optional dedicated/on-prem), and next steps for a pilot. Security and billing integration were primary topics; action items assigned for listing draft, reference arch, and security questionnaire.
topics: Reference architecture for joint solution (hosted + dedicated)
Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we can kick off. Hi Ava, Liam, Priya. hope the time works.
[00:00:18] Ava Martinez: Yup thanks Maya, all good here. want to make sure we get the marketplace checklist + reference arch nailed down.
[00:00:35] Jonah Patel: quick intro from our side, I'm Jonah the SE, I'll own the reference arch and perf targets. we'll be working with your infra team.
[00:01:05] Liam O'Connell: Great, we run SolarisCloud marketplace already for a few ISVs, curious how Redwood fits in — billing, licensing, and whether users can bring their own infra vs managed offering.
[00:01:30] Maya Chen: good callout. Redwood supports hosted API (our SaaS), Dedicated reserved capacity (customer GPU pools), and Private deploy for on-prem/VPC. marketplace listing can link to either: 1) hosted SaaS subscription, 2) listing for dedicated/reserved capacity with an onboarding flow, or 3) reference arch for self-managed.
[00:02:10] Priya Nair: From security we need KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 evidence, and clarifications on data residency when using hosted API. also SSO/SAML and RBAC requirements.
[00:02:45] Rina Gomez: quick note — we have a partner portal template for the listing, and we can provide assets: logos, docs, and a short demo video.
[00:03:12] Ava Martinez: perfect. for billing, SolarisCloud prefers marketplace-native billing (we take payment and pass to partner) but some customers want direct invoice. can Redwood support both?
[00:03:40] Maya Chen: yes we can do marketplace-billing integration for hosted subscriptions, and also provide a reseller/billing mapping for enterprise quotes. we'll share a doc on how SKU mapping works.
[00:04:05] Jonah Patel: on the reference arch — are you imagining a turnkey managed integration where SolarisCloud runs Redwood Dedicated for customers, or a joint reference arch that shows both options?
[00:04:25] Liam O'Connell: we want both: a primary marketplace tile for Redwood-hosted (fastest onboarding) and a secondary reference arch for Dedicated placement where large customers request isolation.
[00:04:50] Maya Chen: that matches our go-to-market. for the reference arch we'll propose: marketplace listing -> onboarding -> optional Dedicated commitment -> network/VPC peering + KMS integration + audit log ship.
[00:05:20] Priya Nair: about KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS or HSM? our compliance team requires the ability to rotate keys and have separate key access.
[00:05:45] Jonah Patel: yes we integrate with customer KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and have a model for HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. there are some constraints on tokenization and cache encryption we can walk through.
[00:06:18] Ava Martinez: can you share sample flow diagrams? also we need to see what telemetry/logs we can ingest into our splunk/observability.
[00:06:40] Rina Gomez: we'll include a reference-arch diagram and a telemetry table. Redwood Console exposes per-route traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[00:07:05] Liam O'Connell: how about network? peering vs private link? some of our customers require private link or direct connect.
[00:07:28] Jonah Patel: we support VPC peering and private link equivalents depending on cloud. for Dedicated we can provision within your region and configure private connectivity. there will be a small network architecture play for NAT, subnets, and KV cache placement.
[00:08:00] Priya Nair: any data retention guarantees for hosted? we need statements for logs, and ability to disable retention for PII.
[00:08:20] Maya Chen: we can provide configurable retention policies; customers can opt into no-retention or limited retention. we'll surface that in the security doc. also for SOC2 evidence we'll share the standard pack.
[00:08:45] Ava Martinez: what about support SLAs for marketplace customers vs direct customers?
[00:09:05] Maya Chen: hosted marketplace customers get standard support tiers; enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) can buy premium SLAs. we'll document the mapping in the listing.
[00:09:30] Jonah Patel: switching to performance — for the pilot we suggest a Dedicated commit with small GPU pool to validate throughput/latency. goal: p95 latency under 400ms for 512-ish tokens using our optimized kernels. that's achievable on A100/TrnX.
[00:10:00] Liam O'Connell: good, our customers mainly care about latency for chat use cases. can we run a benchmark script?
[00:10:18] Jonah Patel: yes we'll provide a benchmark harness and example configs. we'll need sample prompts and expected RPS.
[00:10:40] Ava Martinez: who will run the pilot? Solaris infra or Redwood?
[00:10:55] Maya Chen: joint run — Redwood will provision a test Dedicated slice and provide configs; Solaris will validate in their environment. next step is to agree on perf test plan.
[00:11:25] Rina Gomez: on marketplace artifacts — we need a one-pager, 2 diagrams (deployment + networking), a screenshot of the console, and a short legal blurb.
[00:11:45] Priya Nair: legal blurb should call out the data flow and where customer data resides. also encryption at rest/in transit specifics.
[00:12:10] Jonah Patel: we'll add network flow arrows and label where KV caches live, what gets cached on the serving nodes, and how prefix caching is handled. note: prefix/KV caching can reduce costs but might require sticky sessions for certain models.
[00:12:45] Liam O'Connell: important to surface tradeoffs in the listing — cheaper batched inference vs low-latency single token generation.
[00:13:05] Maya Chen: agreed. we'll include a short FAQ on tradeoffs and recommended profiles for chat vs batch embeddings.
[00:13:30] Ava Martinez: procurement question — does Redwood accept marketplace purchase orders and auto-provision, or do we need manual provisioning?
[00:13:52] Maya Chen: for hosted SaaS yes auto-provisioning can be done. for Dedicated we usually require an onboarding form + capacity planning step before provisioning. marketplace can surface a 'request dedicated' CTA that triggers your sales flow.
[00:14:20] Priya Nair: on compliance, can Redwood provide pen-test reports and third-party attestation?
[00:14:40] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 report, pen-test summary, and responsible disclosure process are available. we'll share links.
[00:15:05] Jonah Patel: quick demo snippet — console screenshot and how to configure model pinning and rollout.
[00:15:25] [screen share noise] Jonah Patel: so here you see a per-route dashboard, cost breakdown by token, and the rollout controls for canary/A-B.
[00:15:55] Ava Martinez: looks good. what about model variants for fallback if capacity is constrained?
[00:16:10] Jonah Patel: we support policy-based routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and can set latency or cost thresholds to trigger fallback.
[00:16:40] Liam O'Connell: is there a way to show expected unit economics in the listing? partners want a simple TCO estimate for customers.
[00:16:58] Rina Gomez: we can include an example TCO calculator and a CSV for customers to upload workload stats.
[00:17:25] Priya Nair: one more from security — audit logs retention and export format specs?
[00:17:40] Jonah Patel: logs export as JSONL to S3 or syslog; retention policies configurable by tenant.
[00:18:05] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[00:18:20] Ava Martinez: quick question — integration with Solaris identity provider for SSO, is SAML supported?
[00:18:35] Maya Chen: yes SAML/SSO supported; we also support SCIM for user provisioning.
[00:18:50] Liam O'Connell: for the pilot, we'll commit to a small Dedicated test for three weeks. need a quote and expected costs.
[00:19:05] Rina Gomez: Rina will draft the marketplace one-pager and assets, Jonah will draft ref-arch, Maya will send security pack.
[00:19:25] Priya Nair: noted, I'll send our network constraints and compliance checklist.
[00:19:40] Maya Chen: perfect. I'll send the marketplace listing draft and SKU mapping by next Tuesday.
[00:20:00] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone, that was efficient. looking forward to the docs.
[00:20:12] Jonah Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with the perf plan and benchmark harness.
[01:00:00] [crosstalk and small side conversation about scheduling follow-up meeting]
[01:15:30] [end of recording]
